asks.model_response: An ionic equation balances every chemical element but has different total charge on each side. Can such an equation represent a complete reaction? The missing condition is charge conservation.

asks.ask: What conservation rule or redox model applies?
asks.why_this_ask: Identify correct oxygen/electron bookkeeping and medium.
asks.model_response: Consider Fe²⁺ oxidation: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻. A permanganate reduction in acidic solution can be expressed as MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O. Each side has one Mn, four O and eight H. Charge on the left is −1 + 8 − 5 = +2, equal to Mn²⁺ on the right. Multiplying the iron half-reaction by five cancels electrons when the two are added.
